en: A bill becomes a law when both the Senate and House of Representatives approve it, and the President signs it.
Dr. Fe del Mundo designed a bamboo incubator that uses warm water in jars to maintain a steady temperature for premature babies.
Andres Bonifacio initiated the Philippine revolution by tearing cedulas, which symbolically broke the Filipinos' forced allegiance to the Spanish colonial government.
The Ifugao build stone-walled rice terraces on mountainsides to capture rainwater and prevent soil erosion for growing irrigated rice.
Filipino citizens exercise their right to suffrage by voting for candidates, which directly determines who holds public office.
The President exercises veto power by rejecting a passed bill, which prevents it from becoming a law unless Congress overrides it.
Participants in the Ati-Atihan festival paint their bodies with black soot to honor the indigenous Ati people who helped early settlers.
The government collects taxes from citizens to fund public services, which provides the money needed to build schools and hospitals.
Ancient Filipinos used the Baybayin writing system by carving specific symbols on bamboo or leaves to record their daily transactions and poetry.
Dr. Alfredo Santos created artificial pearls by molding crushed Capiz shells into spheres, providing a cheaper alternative to natural oyster pearls.
Jose Rizal wrote Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose Spanish abuses, which awakened Filipino nationalism and inspired the revolution.
Communities practice the Bayanihan spirit by physically lifting and moving a traditional nipa hut, which helps a family relocate without paying workers.
